subject: Executive market scan + OKR sync: model release & pricing shifts
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 13 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Exec market scan: fast-moving pricing + open model releases (QBR input)

Team — quick read, flagged for QBR slide deck. Pulled together a short market scan after the weekend:

1) Pricing moves (high priority)
- CompetitorA cut per-token list price on hosted LLM endpoints by ~22% (effective 12/11). They also announced a new reserve-discount program for committed throughput (up to 40% off for 12-mo). See attached competitor-pricing-table-20261210.xlsx.
- CompetitorB is experimenting with per-request micro-bundles (lower baseline for small inference calls). Early field reports show some customers moving non-sensitive routing to micro-bundles.

2) Model releases and positioning
- OpenModelX (v1.5) released with improved long-context handling; early benchmark threads show latency/perf similar to our medium-weight models but at lower token-cost on their hosted infra.
- Vendor CloudVendor announced a managed quantized offering with aggressive marketing around "near-lossless" 4-bit quantization — potential threat to our positioning on high-quality quantized inference. Their partner Olivia Chen looped me in; she offered a partner briefing if we want deeper technical slides.

3) Sales/Field signals
- Rachel Turner (Acme Inc.) pinged sales about a renewal where pricing is the sticking point — they explicitly referenced CompetitorA's new commit discount program. Anthony from DataFirm also flagged a procurement RFP that includes CompetitorA pricing as baseline.

Why this matters for QBR: the combination of headline price cuts + new product combos will show up in field objections and could affect churn on smaller accounts if we don't articulate unit economics and commit alternatives clearly.

Ask: please review the attached 1-pager and pricing table and add one slide (2 bullets) from your org:
- Laura: a crisp 1-line position on why our latency/cost tradeoffs are superior for production use (data point + customer quote if available)
- Aditya: quick note on remediation levers we can offer (temporary credits, committed tier options, targeted quantization profiles)
- Maya: operational impact — how this might affect our throughput/cluster planning if customers move to cheaper micro-bundle routing.

I copied Kimberly because I want this in the leadership QBR appendix; Kimberly can collate. Can we get inputs by EOD Wednesday 12/15?

—Markus

Markus Klein
VP, Product Strategy | Redwood Inference

Thanks — two suggested bullets for the exec slide (I pasted below into the draft PPT):
- "Unit economics: Redwood maintains better sustained throughput for enterprise workloads — our measured 95th percentile latency and customer-reported quality scores mean fewer retries and lower total tokens per session vs. micro-bundles (see customer quote: "Redwood's responses require fewer follow-ups, saving us ~12% on tokens" — Acme Inc.)."
- "Positioning: emphasize committed + observability: we win renewals when customers care about predictable latency, traceability, and SLO-backed SLAs; price alone is a weak signal vs. enterprise-grade guarantees."

Attachments: added a short customer quote extract and linked the Acme renewal thread for context.

-Laura
